title: Panglong
summary: Aung San and leaders from the Shan, Kachin and Chin uplands agreed to seek independence together. The terms of the union itself were left to be settled later.
detail: Panglong is remembered as the founding promise of a federal Burma. It was also a narrow agreement: many communities in the lowlands and the southeast were not party to it. The gap between what Panglong is remembered as promising and what it actually settled has been argued over ever since.
uncertainty: Interpretations of what Panglong committed the union to differ sharply between Bamar-centred and ethnic-nationality accounts.

title: Aung San is assassinated
summary: Aung San and most of his cabinet were shot dead in Yangon, six months before independence.

title: Independence
summary: Burma left the British Empire with a border it had not drawn and a constitutional question it had not answered.

title: The war starts immediately
summary: Communist forces revolted in 1948 and Karen forces in 1949. Armed conflict is older than the independent state, not a later development.
detail: This ordering matters for everything that follows. Accounts that treat ethnic armed conflict as a consequence of the 1962 coup, or of the 2021 coup, have the chronology backwards.
uncertainty: Territorial control in this period is poorly documented. Areas of insurgent activity can be described; front lines cannot.

title: Ne Win takes power
summary: The army dissolved parliament and governed directly. The Burmese Way to Socialism nationalised the economy and closed the country.

title: The Citizenship Law
summary: A new law sorted the population into tiers of citizenship built around recognised national races. Rohingya were not among them.
detail: The law is the legal mechanism behind Rohingya statelessness. Its categories still govern who can hold which documents, and therefore who can move, study, marry and vote.

summary: Demonstrations spread from Yangon through the country and were put down by the army. Thousands are believed to have been killed.
detail: What happened next set a pattern. Activists who could not stay in the cities went to the borderlands, where established ethnic armed organisations already held ground. The All Burma Students Democratic Front was formed there in November.
uncertainty: There is no agreed death toll for 1988. Estimates vary by an order of magnitude depending on source and method.

title: An election, and no transfer of power
summary: The NLD won overwhelmingly. The result was not honoured and power was not transferred.

title: The Saffron Revolution
summary: Monks led demonstrations through the major cities. The response was again lethal force and mass arrest.

title: Cyclone Nargis
summary: A cyclone devastated the Irrawaddy Delta. The government restricted international relief access while proceeding with a constitutional referendum.
uncertainty: [DATA NEEDED: cyclone track geometry and affected-population figures from a citable meteorological and humanitarian source]

title: The 2008 Constitution
summary: A quarter of every legislature was reserved for serving officers, the three security ministries were placed under military control, and amending the document was made to require more than three quarters of parliament.
detail: Read together, those provisions mean the military bloc can block any amendment on its own. Every elected government after 2010 operated inside this frame.

title: A quasi-civilian government
summary: Thein Sein took office. Censorship relaxed, political prisoners were released, and sanctions began to lift.

title: Myitsone is suspended
summary: The government suspended a large Chinese-backed dam in Kachin State after sustained domestic opposition.
detail: The suspension signalled that the new government would respond to domestic opinion, and it introduced the pattern that runs through the rest of this story: Chinese investment, local objection, and a government caught between them.

title: Violence in Rakhine
summary: Communal violence displaced tens of thousands, and many Rohingya were moved into camps they were not free to leave.
uncertainty: [DATA NEEDED: displacement figures and camp locations with as-of dates]

title: The Nationwide Ceasefire Agreement
summary: Eight organisations signed. Several of the largest did not, and some were excluded from the talks entirely.
detail: The word nationwide describes the ambition, not the coverage. Reading the agreement as a national settlement obscures who was left outside it.
uncertainty: [DATA NEEDED: confirm the full signatory and non-signatory lists, including organisations that signed after 2015, against the agreement text]

title: The NLD wins
summary: A decisive NLD victory produced a government that still could not command the army, appoint the security ministers, or amend the constitution.
detail: Barred from the presidency by a constitutional clause, Aung San Suu Kyi governed as State Counsellor. The arrangement is the clearest illustration of the hybrid: an elected majority operating around a reserved military domain rather than over it.
uncertainty: [DATA NEEDED: verified 2015 seat counts by party and chamber before building the comparative seat visualisation]

title: Northern Rakhine
summary: Military operations in northern Rakhine drove several hundred thousand Rohingya across the border into Bangladesh within weeks.
detail: The displacement concentrated around Cox's Bazar, which became one of the largest refugee settlements in the world. UN human rights bodies documented the conduct of the operations; Myanmar has rejected their characterisation.
uncertainty: [DATA NEEDED: registered refugee totals with as-of dates from UNHCR, rather than the round figures in general circulation]

title: The Gambia goes to the ICJ
summary: The Gambia filed proceedings against Myanmar under the Genocide Convention. Aung San Suu Kyi appeared at The Hague to contest the case.
uncertainty: The case record establishes that proceedings exist and their procedural history. It is not a finding on the merits.

title: The NLD wins again
summary: The NLD increased its majority. The military-aligned USDP rejected the result and alleged large-scale fraud.
detail: Election observers and the election commission did not find irregularities on anything approaching the scale alleged. The fraud claim became the stated justification for what happened twelve weeks later.
uncertainty: [DATA NEEDED: verified 2020 seat counts by party and chamber, plus the list of townships where voting was cancelled]

title: The coup
summary: Hours before the newly elected parliament was to convene, the army detained Aung San Suu Kyi, President Win Myint and others, declared a state of emergency, and handed power to the Commander-in-Chief.
detail: The elected legislature never sat. A State Administration Council was announced the following day. The justification offered was the fraud allegation that observers had not substantiated.

title: The hospitals stop first
summary: Hospital staff refused to work under the new authorities. Within weeks teachers, railway workers, bank staff and civil servants had joined them.
detail: The Civil Disobedience Movement went after the state's capacity to function rather than its capacity for violence. A government that cannot run its railways, clear its payments or staff its ministries is a government with a problem no amount of force solves.
uncertainty: Participation was never reliably counted. Sector-level accounts are well documented; national totals are estimates.

title: The parliament that was not allowed to sit
summary: MPs elected in November formed a committee asserting that they, not the council in Naypyidaw, were the lawful legislature.

title: The streets
summary: Demonstrations spread through Yangon, Mandalay, Naypyidaw and towns across the country, drawing in people with no previous political involvement.

title: The response hardens
summary: Security forces moved from arrests to live fire. March 2021 included some of the deadliest days since 1988.
detail: AAPP, which counts only cases it can individually verify, maintained the most-cited running tally. Its figures are explicitly a documented floor rather than an estimate of the true total.
uncertainty: [DATA NEEDED: AAPP documented killings and detentions with the as-of date attached, rather than a figure quoted without one]

title: The Federal Democracy Charter
summary: The opposition published a framework that abolished the 2008 constitution on its own terms and set out an interim federal structure.
detail: The charter is the document that turns a protest movement into a constitutional project. It creates the consultative council, the interim executive, and the language of federal democracy that the rest of the period argues about.

title: The National Unity Government
summary: An interim executive was announced, drawn from elected MPs together with ethnic and civil society figures.
detail: The NUG is the most internationally visible face of the opposition. It is not, however, the command structure of the resistance, and treating it as one is the most common way of misreading what follows.

title: The People's Defence Force
summary: The NUG announced an armed force. In practice the name covered a very large number of locally raised groups with varying relationships to it.
uncertainty: Strength estimates differ by an order of magnitude depending on whether locally raised units are counted.

title: The same road as 1988
summary: People who could not stay in the cities travelled to the borderlands, where established armed organisations trained them. The route was the one taken in 1988.
detail: The parallel is structural rather than exact. In 1988 those who left were overwhelmingly students; after 2021 they included doctors, engineers, police and civil servants, and the organisations receiving them had thirty more years of institutional depth.
uncertainty: Routes are shown as directional flows between regions, not as tracked journeys. Individual movements are not documented at that resolution.

title: A people's defensive war
summary: The NUG declared a defensive war. Fighting was already widespread in Sagaing, Magway, Chin and Karenni.
uncertainty: Conflict events indicate where fighting occurred. They do not indicate who held the ground, and are not used here to infer control.

title: Who is the resistance?
summary: Not one organisation. A consultative council, an interim executive, hundreds of local defence groups, and ethnic armed organisations older than the state itself.
detail: The relationships between them are negotiated and variable. Some units answer to the NUG. Some answer to an ethnic armed organisation. Some answer to their township. Drawing this as a hierarchy would be simpler and would be wrong.

title: Government from below
summary: Where military administration withdrew, something had to replace it. Townships organised schooling, clinics and dispute resolution, and in places those arrangements grew into state-level executives.
detail: This is the part of the post-coup period that armed-conflict coverage tends to miss. The revolution has been an experiment in building administration as much as a military campaign, and Karenni is the clearest case.
uncertainty: How far these administrations reach, and how contested their authority is, varies by township and is not uniformly documented.

title: Operation 1027
summary: Three allied organisations attacked across northern Shan State, taking towns, bases and border crossings on the route to China.
detail: The significance was not only territorial. It demonstrated that coordinated action could take and hold fixed positions, and it put the most valuable overland trade corridor to China into play.
uncertainty: [DATA NEEDED: township-level control changes with dates and confidence levels, from IISS or SAC-M rather than from press reports of individual battles]

title: The earthquake
summary: A major earthquake struck central Myanmar, with severe damage around Sagaing and Mandalay, in the middle of an active war.
detail: Disaster response in a contested country is a political act: who is allowed to deliver aid, and to whom, becomes part of the conflict.
uncertainty: [DATA NEEDED: magnitude, epicentre, affected-population and casualty figures from USGS and UN OCHA with as-of dates]
